'''Subramaniam Ramakrishnan''' (born 1960) is an Indian [[Polymer chemistry|polymer chemist]], a professor at the Department of Inorganic and Physical Chemistry<ref name="Inorganic and Physical Chemistry">{{Cite web |url=http://ipc.iisc.ac.in/raman.php |title=Inorganic and Physical Chemistry |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> and the designer at the Macromolecular Design and Synthesis Group of the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="Macromolecular Design & Synthesis Group">{{Cite web |url=http://ipc.iisc.ernet.in/~raman/ |title=Macromolecular Design & Synthesis Group |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> He is known for his studies on design and synthesis of controlled polymer structures<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=254 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> and is an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Ramakrishnan,_Prof._Subramaniam |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2005, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Mumbai university,admin block,Tamil Nadu490.jpg|thumb|235px|left|Mumbai University]]
Subramaniam Ramakrishnan, born on 27 August 1960, graduated in chemistry from the [[SIES College of Arts, Science & Commerce]] of  [[Mumbai University]] in 1980. He joined the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay]] to complete his master's degree in 1982.<ref name="Designer">{{Cite web |url=http://ipc.iisc.ernet.in/~raman/resume.html |title=Designer |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> Moving to the US, he secured a PhD from the [[University of Massachusetts, Amherst]] in 1988, working under the guidance of J. C. W. Chien, and did his post-doctoral studies at the Corporate Research Laboratory of the [[Exxon Research and Engineering Company]], New Jersey during 1988–90.<ref name="Distinguished Alumnus">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitb.ac.in/alumni/en/awards/2015/distinguished-alumnus/prof-s-ramakrishnan |title=Distinguished Alumnus |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science Alumni}}</ref> Returning to India, he started his career at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] the same year as a lecturer where he heads the Macromolecular Design and Synthesis Group as the chief designer.<ref name="Macromolecular Design & Synthesis Group" /> http://ipc.iisc.ac.in/~rk/ During his tenure at the IISc, he held the positions of an assistant professor (1993–99) and an associate professor (1999–2005) before becoming a professor of the department of Inorganic and Physical Chemistry in 2005.<ref name="Inorganic and Physical Chemistry" /> In between, he had two stints abroad, first as a visiting scientist at the [[University of Florida]] (2000) and the next, as a Philips Visiting Professor at [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (2001).<ref name="Designer" />  Prof. Ramakrishnan also served as the deputy director<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iisc.ac.in/about/administration/deputy-directors/|title=Indian Institute of Science|website=www.iisc.ac.in|language=en|access-date=2018-06-04}}</ref> at the Indian Institute of Science (2017-2019).

== Legacy and honors ==
Ramakrishnan's research is focused on the study of molecularly designed polymeric materials and the development of synthetic routes such as the transetherification route developed by his team for preparing segmented [[polyethylene oxide]] and their analogues to be used as solid [[polymer electrolytes]].<ref name="Inorganic and Physical Chemistry" /> He is known to have succeeded in designing and synthesizing controlled polymer structures with predetermined properties.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> His team has also demonstrated that the physical properties of [[conjugated polymers]] can be modulated by tuning the average molecular conjugation length. He has documented his research by way of chapters in books edited by others<ref name="RaoMüller2006">{{cite book|author1=C. N. R. Rao|author2=Achim Müller|author3=Anthony K. Cheetham|title=The Chemistry of Nanomaterials: Synthesis, Properties and Applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XjB43Kt-HXYC&pg=PR20|date=24 January 2006|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-3-527-60417-3|pages=20–}}</ref><ref name="Chapter 15. Nanostructured Polymers">{{Cite book |title=Chapter 15. Nanostructured Polymers |pages=476–517 |date=2004 |publisher=Wiley-VCH Verlag GmbH |doi=10.1002/352760247X.ch15|chapter = Nanostructured Polymers|last1 = Ramakrishnan|first1 = S.|isbn=9783527602476 }}</ref> and as peer-reviewed articles;<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Ramakrishnan=3ASubramaniam=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[Google Scholar]], an online repository of scientific articles has listed 121 of them.<ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=Iz8zEQ4AAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2016 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref>

Ramakrishnan received the Bronze Medal of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]]<ref name="CRSI Bronze Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-1999-2008 |title=CRSI Bronze Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Chemical Research Society of India}}</ref> and the MRSI Medal of the Material Research Society of India in 2002.<ref name="Awards and honors">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mrsi.org.in/awardshonours.php |title=Awards and honors |date=2016 |publisher=Material Research Society of India}}</ref> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2005<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> and he was elected as a fellow by the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref name="Fellow profile" />
